h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: An identity on 0->3 forms a residual wrapper around a conv-processed deep route, which eases optimisation and complements rather than dilutes the conv features.
When one output branch is already pooled, a second pooled branch adds a largely redundant smoothed signal, so its marginal harm saturates and is smaller.
When node 1 is an identity copy, a 3x3 on 1->2 provides the first real processing on that route, so it adds more fresh capacity than when node 1 is already conv-processed.
A 3x3 on 0->2 already supplies conv capacity at node 2, so a parallel conv on 1->2 is partly substitutable and gains less.
An identity-like route via 1->3 compensates for losing the 0->3 shortcut, so converting edge 3 to a conv adds capacity without as much trainability cost.
With an input identity into node 3, a conv on 2->3 sits inside a residual block, which makes the added depth trainable and more beneficial.
An input identity into node 3 turns the 1->3 conv path into a residual branch, whose gain exceeds that of a plain stacked conv.
With no direct 0->3 edge, an identity into node 2 gives the deep route unprocessed input and a short gradient path, which the cell otherwise lacks.
A conv on 0->1 feeding a conv on 1->3 forms a deeper conv-conv path to the output, so processing at node 1 is used directly by a learned op.
If node 1 is conv-processed, a skip on 1->3 forwards useful features to the output, whereas if node 1 is a plain copy the skip only duplicates the input.
